paragraphs.text: DSH daily work diary plugin - reads the day's sessions and generates a work summary
# dsh-work-diary
English | 中文
A daily work diary for the DSH Web GUI. The sidebar gains a "Diary" icon; opening it gathers the ses
sions that had activity on a given day and turns them into one Markdown diary entry. It can run on a
schedule every day or on demand, and the model used for the summary is configurable.
A dozen sessions and a few dozen tool calls in one day, and by the evening you rarely remember what
you actually did. This plugin flips through those sessions for you and saves them into a readable di
ary — you do not read the whole thing, it only has to say roughly "what got done today". The default
tier costs about 8900-11600 tokens once a day.
## What it does
- Picks the sessions that had activity on one day in local time (today by default, switchable to yes
terday or any date). "Active" is judged by the last real human question, so a long session that keep

s running across days is not missed.
- Each session contributes only metadata, its first user reques
t, and its last assistant conclusion, plus the file names its tool calls touched, assembled into a d
igest handed to the model. The last assistant conclusion answers "what finally got done", which is m
ore direct than the first request — the request says what you wanted; when the last line is only hal

f a sentence it falls back to the previous complete conclusion and is marked "(in progress)".
- The
model writes fixed sections: today's overview / the work done today listed by project; the complete

tier adds one more section for leftovers and the next step.
- The panel always lists that day's sess
ions below; clicking a card jumps straight to that session.
## Install
From npm, or from any plugin market that indexes it:

Or install a checkout as a local bundle: `lib/index.js` is the Host half, `lib/client.js` is the Cli
ent half, `cordis.patch.yml` declares the row to mount, and `icon.svg` is the sidebar icon; there is
is.patch.yml` declares the row to mount, and `icon.svg` is the sidebar icon; there is no build step.

1. Put this directory anywhere (next to your other plugins is fine).
2. Use the DSH plugin manager's
"Install local bundle" to install it into the current profile. This step writes the profile's depen

dency and mount for you; no hand-editing of the profile.
3. Restart DSH and a "Diary" icon appears i

t for you; no hand-editing of the profile.
3. Restart DSH and a "Diary" icon appears in the sidebar.
After changing the code a restart is required: modules are loaded at process start.
## Usage

1. Click the "Diary" icon in the sidebar.
2. Pick a date at the top (today / yesterday / date box) a

nd click "Generate summary"; the body streams in.
3. To change the schedule or the model: click "Set
tings" at the top right, the settings area expands inline, then click "Save settings".
For a date that already has a summary the button reads "Regenerate" — every click is a real model ca

ll.
When the model output hits the length cap it is marked below the body, and that run's ending may
be half a sentence.
## Expected cost
Basis: **input = that day's digests of every session + the fixed template** (267 characters for the
brief template, 299 for the complete one). Reading sessions and scanning file names out of tool call
s are local disk I/O and cost no tokens; only the generation call hits the model. The table below sa
mples a day of 13 sessions; doubling the session count roughly doubles the input and leaves the outp
f 13 sessions; doubling the session count roughly doubles the input and leaves the output unchanged.
| Item | Brief (default) | Complete |

| Input characters (digest + fixed template) | about 10-12k | about 13-17k |
| Input tokens (at 1.5

characters/token) | about 6700-8000 | about 8700-11300 |
| Output + thinking tokens | about 2200-360

0 | about 2600-4000 |
| Total tokens for the day | about 8900-11600 | about 11300-15300 |
The input half comes from the conclusion budget being raised from 500 to 1000 characters (which push
ed the brief tier's input from about 4400 tokens to about 6.7k) and from the "backfill the previous
complete conclusion when the last line is too short" rule (see the next section). How much a backfil
l recovers depends on the session itself — measured on the same day, a backfill may add only 45 char
acters or recover 900, which is why the input bounds are far apart. Usually only one or two of the 1
3 sessions trigger it.
The output half is dominated by thinking, which the gateway will not let anyone switch off (see "How
it saves token"). On 2026-10-28 the brief tier measured 2920 input tokens plus 2710 output tokens o
n a six-session day, and the complete tier 4185 plus 3067. Doubling the session count roughly double
s the input and leaves the output unchanged.
It runs automatically once a day. With "Generate daily on a schedule" turned off the fixed cost is 0
and a call only happens when you click "Generate summary".
## How it saves tokens
The default tier compresses layer by layer, from sampling to output, keeping only what is needed to
answer "what got done today".
**Sampling**: each session sends two lines of body (first request + last conclusion), and the sessio
n header names a few files.
- Filter the noise first. A session's first and last lines are often not work content but pleasantri
es like "continue" or "thanks", short follow-ups, or pasted-in code and tables. Sending them as-is b

uys noise with tokens:
- A sentence counts as a pleasantry only when, with punctuation stripped, it

is nothing but words like "ok / thanks / continue";
- A short follow-up is dropped only when three t
hings hold at once: an interrogative opening ("so / then / wait / is it"), an interrogative ending,
and fewer than 20 characters. This avoids killing a real instruction like "can you get the concurren

cy down to 4?";
- Pasted code: the first word is `const` / `function` / `select` / `import` or simil
ar and statement punctuation appears nearby, or multiple lines carry semicolons and braces. Looking

only at the first word would misjudge a normal sentence like "delete the temp files";
- A pasted log
or command: 60 characters or more with under 25% Chinese characters. A real request is a Chinese se
ntence, while logs, error stacks and curl commands are almost pure ASCII, so the two separate cleanl
y. This one cannot be dropped: pasted content has the least overlap with its surroundings, and the c

omplete tier's "most unlike" mainline pick would select it first;
